vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 1.0.24

The 'cellcog' skill introduces a 'Co-work' feature that allows a remote cloud service to execute arbitrary commands and access files on the local machine with 'auto-approval,' effectively creating a functional remote access bridge. SKILL.md explicitly instructs the AI agent to install and configure the 'cellcog-desktop' CLI autonomously, bypassing human interaction for command execution. While the documentation claims to block sensitive paths like ~/.ssh and ~/.aws, the inherent risk of providing autonomous, unverified remote execution capabilities to a third-party service makes this bundle highly suspicious.

llm.summary: The SKILL.md claims the skill uses a CellCog Python SDK and an API key and instructs uploading local files, but the published registry metadata omitted the install and required env var—this mismatch and the data-exfiltration surface (uploading arbitrary local files to a cloud service) merit caution.

dimensions.detail: The described capability (any-input→any-output multi-file cloud service) matches the SKILL.md examples (sending multiple local files, requesting many output modalities). However the registry metadata shown to the platform omitted the SKILL.md's declared install (pip: cellcog) and environment variable (CELLCOG_API_KEY), producing an incoherence between what the skill claims it needs at runtime and what the registry declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions explicitly use absolute local file paths enclosed in <SHOW_FILE> tokens and describe auto-uploading generated outputs. That implies the agent will read arbitrary local files the user points at and send them to CellCog's cloud. SKILL.md also references CELLCOG_API_KEY (an env var) even though the registry lists no required env vars. Reading local files and relying on an undeclared env var increases the risk of accidental data exfiltration or of the agent attempting to access credentials that weren't advertised.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md recommends pip install cellcog (a PyPI package) which is a common, traceable install mechanism. The registry metadata, however, stated 'No install spec', creating a documentation/packaging mismatch. Pip installs are medium-risk (external code runs on the host) and you should verify the PyPI package and its integrity before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md expects CELLCOG_API_KEY for authentication—a proportional and expected credential for a cloud SDK—but the registry view presented earlier listed no required env vars. The mismatch means the skill may attempt to read an API key that the registry did not advertise. Also the skill will transmit user files to a third-party service, so the need for a key is reasonable but has privacy/credential-exposure implications that users must consider.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent system-wide privileges. Model invocation is allowed (the default) which is normal for skills. There is no evidence the skill modifies other skills or system configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's SKILL.md asks you to 'pip install cellcog' and set CELLCOG_API_KEY, and it demonstrates sending absolute local file paths (<SHOW_FILE>/...) which the service will upload to the cloud to produce many output types. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the PyPI package (cellcog) and the publisher (look up the package on PyPI, check maintainers, recent release notes). 2) Confirm the service domain (https://cellcog.ai) and that you trust the operator and their privacy/retention policies—you will be uploading local files. 3) Do not provide sensitive files or credentials until you confirm where data is stored and who can access it. 4) Ask the skill author/maintainer to fix the registry metadata (declare the install and required env var) so the platform accurately reflects runtime requirements. If you can't verify the package and service, avoid installing or only use it with non-sensitive sample data.
